title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #1

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you do before acting on a spoken instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to all of it
   B. Move at once
   C. Laugh
   D. Look away

2. What is polite when you collect a song from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Take the song without asking
   B. Refuse to listen
   C. Greet them and thank them at the end
   D. Interrupt while they sing

3. How should you find out how your mother tongue forms plurals? (1 mark)
   A. Add s to every word
   B. Ignore it
   C. Guess from English
   D. Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher

4. What does fluent reading mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   B. Skipping words
   C. Reading very slowly word by word
   D. Reading in a whisper

5. What should you leave between two words? (1 mark)
   A. A whole line
   B. No space
   C. A picture
   D. A finger space

6. When copying a sentence, what should you check? (1 mark)
   A. Only the colour of the pen
   B. Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   C. Only the date
   D. Only the page number

7. Which of these is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. The door was open.
   B. Close the door.
   C. The door is red.
   D. A door has a handle.

8. Which instruction is clearer? (1 mark)
   A. Do the thing.
   B. Go and do it.
   C. Put it there.
   D. Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.

9. What should you do first when you give an instruction to a friend? (1 mark)
   A. Plan the steps in order
   B. Walk away
   C. Say all steps at once quickly
   D. Shout

10. Which sentence uses a comma correctly for speaking to someone? (1 mark)
   A. Wanjiku please bring the, umbrella.
   B. Wanjiku please bring, the umbrella.
   C. Wanjiku please, bring the umbrella
   D. Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.

11. What is a resource person? (1 mark)
   A. A pupil who is late
   B. A kind of book
   C. A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   D. A bag for books

12. Why do we listen to oral texts about safety? (1 mark)
   A. To count the words
   B. To sleep
   C. To learn how to stay safe
   D. To waste time

13. In the story of Otieno, what caused his burn? (1 mark)
   A. He touched the handle of the hot pot
   B. He played with a dog
   C. He fell from a tree
   D. He ate hot food

14. Where can you check the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. In a bag
   B. In a simple dictionary
   C. On a clock
   D. On a shoe

15. What is a word puzzle used for? (1 mark)
   A. Painting
   B. Running
   C. Cooking
   D. Practising vocabulary in a fun way

16. Which word shows the last step in a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. Next
   B. Finally
   C. Begin
   D. First

17. Where can a class publish its final paragraphs? (1 mark)
   A. In a school or class magazine
   B. In the dustbin
   C. Under a bed
   D. On a stone

18. Why do we put ideas in order? (1 mark)
   A. To confuse the reader
   B. So the reader can follow them
   C. To make the story shorter
   D. To use more words

19. What is the lesson of the hare and tortoise story? (1 mark)
   A. Hares are lazy
   B. Slow and steady wins the race
   C. Tortoises are fast
   D. Never race

20. Which is a part of an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A stamp
   B. A page number
   C. The ending
   D. A price tag

21. How should you collect proverbs from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Refuse to listen
   B. Take it without asking
   C. Interrupt
   D. Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb

22. Which strategy would you use to see what a newspaper article is about? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting
   B. Scanning for a number
   C. Painting
   D. Skimming

23. What should you keep in mind when scanning? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A poem
   C. What you are looking for
   D. Nothing

24. A seller buys mangoes for 300 shillings and sells them for 450 shillings. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. 150 shillings
   B. 300 shillings
   C. 450 shillings
   D. 750 shillings

25. Which word shows a choice? (1 mark)
   A. so
   B. and
   C. or
   D. but

26. What is the subject of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Who or what the sentence is about
   B. The verb only
   C. What is said about it
   D. The full stop

27. Which word joins two ideas that contrast? (1 mark)
   A. because
   B. but
   C. and
   D. so

28. What is animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   B. Hunting animals
   C. Selling animals only
   D. Ignoring animals

29. What is a talent? (1 mark)
   A. A skill you are good at
   B. A kind of food
   C. A book
   D. A rule

30. What does an interjection show? (1 mark)
   A. A sudden feeling
   B. A time
   C. A number
   D. A place

31. In the sentence Oops, it is torn, what is the interjection? (1 mark)
   A. Oops
   B. is
   C. torn
   D. it

32. What is a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A list
   C. A conversation between two or more people
   D. A long description

33. Which describes an object by size and colour? (1 mark)
   A. A big red bag
   B. Bagging
   C. To bag
   D. A bag

34. Which word in an advert may be used to persuade? (1 mark)
   A. door
   B. table
   C. paper
   D. best

35. Which question should you ask about an advert? (1 mark)
   A. What is the paper colour?
   B. How many pages does it have?
   C. What is being sold and how much does it cost?
   D. Who cut it?

36. What should you use to fill a form unless told otherwise? (1 mark)
   A. A chalk
   B. A crayon
   C. A pen
   D. A finger

37. Which pair of verbs shows an action? (1 mark)
   A. red, blue
   B. table, chair
   C. is, are
   D. vote, count

38. What should you do when someone else is speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Talk over them
   B. Leave
   C. Draw
   D. Listen without interrupting

39. What should you add when a task is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. A warning
   B. A song
   C. A joke
   D. A colour

40. What is an instruction chart? (1 mark)
   A. A list of animals
   B. A story chart
   C. A poster showing steps for a task
   D. A drawing of a house

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three tips for telling a story well. (3 marks)

42. Explain why you should not share personal details on a form without asking an adult. (3 marks)

43. Describe the steps in writing a story from a picture. (4 marks)

44. Give two rules for looking after class library books. (2 marks)

45. Give three rules for good turn taking. (3 marks)

46. Add capital letters, commas and full stops: on friday we bought rice beans and flour (3 marks)

47. Copy this sentence correctly: the food is hot (2 marks)

48. Name three questions to ask yourself before telling a personal experience. (3 marks)

49. Write one simile and one metaphor about a teacher. (3 marks)

50. Give three steps for telling a story fluently. (3 marks)

51. Give two sequence words. (2 marks)

52. Explain two differences between an advert and a news item. (4 marks)

53. Give the meaning of comprehension and say why it matters when we listen. (2 marks)

54. Play the role of the soloist in a singing game. Write three short instructions you would sing and say what the group should do for each. (5 marks)

55. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

56. Mama Neema buys a box of bananas for 200 shillings and sells it for 260 shillings. Find her profit. (2 marks)

57. Plan a short oral narrative about a school rule. Say the characters, the events, the ending, and where you will use a simile and a metaphor. (5 marks)

58. Give two reasons why neat handwriting matters. (2 marks)

59. Explain what an instruction chart is. (2 marks)

60. Give two adjectives to describe a school bag in an advert. (2 marks)

61. Give three rules for writing clear instructions. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Listen to all of it
   Listening to the end helps you act correctly.

2. C — Greet them and thank them at the end
   Good manners include greeting, listening and thanking.

3. D — Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   Languages form plurals in different ways, so we ask people who know the language well.

4. A — Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

5. D — A finger space
   A finger width keeps words clear.

6. B — Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   These are the points of neat copying.

7. B — Close the door.
   Close the door tells you what to do.

8. D — Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.
   It says what, where and why.

9. A — Plan the steps in order
   Planning helps to give clear instructions.

10. D — Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   A comma follows the name of the person addressed.

11. C — A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   A nurse visiting a class is an example of a resource person.

12. C — To learn how to stay safe
   Safety texts teach what to do and what to avoid.

13. A — He touched the handle of the hot pot
   He moved closer and touched the handle, and the pot tipped.

14. B — In a simple dictionary
   Dictionaries give meanings.

15. D — Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   Puzzles help pupils remember words.

16. B — Finally
   Finally is used for the last step.

17. A — In a school or class magazine
   Publishing shares the writing.

18. B — So the reader can follow them
   Order makes writing clear.

19. B — Slow and steady wins the race
   The tortoise wins by steady effort.

20. C — The ending
   Stories have openings, characters, events and endings.

21. D — Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb
   Politeness and careful listening are important.

22. D — Skimming
   You want the main idea.

23. C — What you are looking for
   Scanning needs a target.

24. A — 150 shillings
   450 minus 300 is 150.

25. C — or
   Or offers a choice.

26. A — Who or what the sentence is about
   The subject is the topic of the sentence.

27. B — but
   But shows contrast.

28. A — Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   Welfare means care for animals' well-being.

29. A — A skill you are good at
   A talent is a natural ability.

30. A — A sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotions.

31. A — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

32. C — A conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue is people talking.

33. A — A big red bag
   Big and red are adjectives.

34. D — best
   Words such as best persuade people to buy.

35. C — What is being sold and how much does it cost?
   Buyers check product and price.

36. C — A pen
   A pen gives clear permanent writing.

37. D — vote, count
   Vote and count are actions.

38. D — Listen without interrupting
   Respectful listening is key.

39. A — A warning
   Warnings keep people safe.

40. C — A poster showing steps for a task
   It shows steps in order.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Start with a clear opening, tell events in order, speak clearly, look at the audience, end with what you learned.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Someone could misuse the details, so a trusted adult should check that it is safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the risk, one for asking an adult, one for a clear explanation.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, ask who where and what, plan the characters, setting, problem and ending, write the story in order, and check it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Turn pages gently, never write in them, return them on time, keep them clean (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wait for the speaker to finish, keep your turn short, do not always speak first, listen politely.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: On Friday we bought rice, beans and flour.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capitals, one mark for the commas, one for the full stop.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: The food is hot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the capital letter and one mark for the full stop.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who was there, what happened, where, when, why, how did I feel.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each question.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Simile: The teacher is as patient as a rock. Metaphor: The teacher is a walking dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a simile, one for a metaphor, one for clearly showing the difference.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Know the story well, speak clearly, keep a steady pace, change your voice for characters, look at the audience, end with the lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, finally (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: An advert aims to persuade people to buy, while news informs about events. An advert gives a price and where to buy, while news gives who, what, where and when.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for each difference.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Comprehension means understanding. It matters because we can then remember and use what we heard.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for why it matters.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three clear instructions with matching actions, for example Clap two times (the group claps twice), Stir the pot (the group pretends to stir), Turn around (the group turns).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for each matching response, with a total of five marks for three well matched pairs and correct listening steps.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is quick reading for the main idea and scanning is quick searching for a specific fact.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: 260 minus 200 equals 60 shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the working and one mark for the answer with units.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any plan with characters, events in order, an ending with a lesson, and one simile and one metaphor, for example a pupil who came late but learned that rules are like a map.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, events, ending, simile and metaphor.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader to understand the message, and it shows respect and builds confidence.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible reason.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: An instruction chart is a poster that shows the steps of a task in order using short words and often pictures.
   Working / marking points: One mark for steps in order and one for a poster or pictures.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: strong, big, red, light, new (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each adjective.

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put steps in order, begin each step with a verb, use short sentences, one action per step, add warnings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
